transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's medication-safety huddle. As you know, the hospital introduced the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol this past Monday, and before we allow it to be used on the upcoming night shift, I need to hear from each of you about any operational findings or concerns. I'll be making the final decision on whether any temporary safety safeguards are needed this afternoon, so I'd like to start by hearing from pharmacy, laboratory medicine, nursing education, and clinical IT. Who would like to go first?

As a potential safeguard, pharmacy can remove the bedside stock from the automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold.

transcript.text: From laboratory medicine, I need to flag an important operational issue. Our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. I want everyone to be aware of this so we can factor it into any safety safeguards Morgan decides on this afternoon.

transcript.text: From nursing education, I need to flag a significant staffing concern. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not yet completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Under our current policy, each of those nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they can administer this medication. This could create operational bottlenecks and safety risks tonight if the protocol goes forward without additional safeguards.

transcript.text: Thank you all for those thorough reports. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make my decision this afternoon. Leah, pharmacy has identified three concentration-selection errors between the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL strengths, and you're proposing we pull bedside stock from the ADCs and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes as a temporary safeguard. Ravi, lab medicine's anti-Xa analyzer won't be available for calibration until Friday at 17:00, so the approved alternative is aPTT monitoring every six hours in the interim. Tessa, 18 nurses on tonight's shift haven't completed the administration module, meaning each would need charge-nurse sign-off, which could create bottlenecks and safety risks. And Jon, clinical IT can deploy a concentration-selection alert at 16:00 today requiring clinician acknowledgment before order release. These are all significant findings. I'm going to consider each of these carefully and will issue my decision on temporary safety safeguards this afternoon before the night shift begins. Are there any additional details or concerns anyone would like to add before I finalize my review?

decisions.safety_protocol: The intravenous anticoagulant protocol may proceed on the upcoming night shift with temporary safety safeguards in place, given the operational findings reported.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: Pharmacy will remove bedside stock of both concentrations from automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes to eliminate concentration-selection errors. Leah confirmed these can be ready and distributed before the night shift begins.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: aPTT monitoring every six hours will be used as the approved alternative to the unavailable anti-Xa analyzer until calibration is complete on Friday at 17:00. Ravi confirmed lab staff are prepared to handle the testing volume.
decisions.nurse_authorization: The 18 nurses who have not completed the administration module will require charge-nurse sign-off before administering this medication, per current policy. Tessa will brief charge nurses on sign-off expectations and the monitoring change, and will coordinate with pharmacy on labeling and communication to support those nurses.
decisions.electronic_alert: Clinical IT will deploy the high-priority concentration-selection alert at 16:00 today, requiring clinician acknowledgment before the order can be released, as an additional safeguard.

commitments.detail: Remove bedside stock from ADCs and prepare and distribute pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes before the night shift begins. Coordinate with nursing education on labeling and communication.
Ensure aPTT monitoring every six hours is operational for tonight's shift and handle testing volume until the anti-Xa analyzer is calibrated on Friday at 17:00.

Brief charge nurses on sign-off expectations for the 18 nurses who have not completed the module, incorporate the aPTT six-hour monitoring cadence into nurse communications, and coordinate with pharmacy on labeling.
Deploy the high-priority concentration-selection alert at 16:00 today requiring clinician acknowledgment before order release.
